newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen drifting higher in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen drifting higher in Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar is expected to edge higher against the yen and the mark in Asia on Tuesday, with a mark buying spree fading after a left-wing victory in the first round of the French election raised concern about a weak Euro.

The unexpected left-wing victory spurred a wave of mark buying against major currencies on Monday in Tokyo, but it also raised speculation later that Paris may seek softer membership criteria for the single European currency and prompted mark selling against the dollar in Europe, dealers said. "Since the dollar/mark partly recovered, the dollar is likely to edge higher against the yen," a dealer at a trust bank said.

Dealers said they were focusing on whether Japanese exporters and others would move to sell dollars for yen at around 116.50 yen. The downside could be supported by buying interest by some Japanese investors, they said.
The trust bank dealer said there would be selling interest on rises from Japanese exporters but they may back off their offers if the dollar shows signs of rising further.
"Exporters are in no rush to sell dollars," he said.
He added that the dollar rose as high as around 116.72 yen in Toronto on Monday amid a markets holiday in Britain and the United States.
There has been market talk that Japanese public funds were placing bids on the downside, and some dealers said they had bought dollars for yen recently.

The trust bank dealer said private pension funds were seen ready to buy dollars on dips, but added that there was also a possibility that they would sell off dollars for hedging if the greenback tumbled sharply.
A city bank dealer said mark buying interest would probably continue amid a lack of market-moving factors. He said he would mainly focus on movements of European currencies.
